sentences.text: The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 23.06.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Shahabuddin, learned counsel assisted by Shri Ram Kumar Pandey, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Shravan Kumar Dubey, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. Learned counsel for the applicant contests the minority of the victim as depicted in the prosecution case.
2. The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 17 years of age in the F.I.R. only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant contests the age of the victim set out in the prosecution case in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P.
and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.
(ii) The age of the victim was incorrectly got registered in the school records by the victim's parents to give her an advantage in life.

entities.text:
Monish Vs. State of U.P.
and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The school certificate showing her age as 12 years is not reliable.
(iii) The victim in her statements under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has asserted that she is 12 years of age.
(iv) The medical report drawn up to determine the age of the victim opines that she is 18 years of age.
The victim is in fact a major.
4. The victim and the applicant were intimate.
5. The F.I.R. is the result of opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship.
6. The victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has admitted to intimacy with the applicant.
She has asserted that she eloped with the applicant to Muzaffarpur, Bihar of her own volition.
The victim has clearly stated that she got married to the applicant of her own free will.
7. No allegation of wrongful detention, abduction, inappropriate behaviour or commission or rape has been made by the victim against the applicant in the aforesaid statement.
8. False and aggravated allegations were made under Section 164 Cr.P.C. by the victim at the behest of her parents to save the failing prosecution case and to deflect attention from her own conduct.

sentences.text: 9. Major inconsistencies in the FIR, the statement under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. discredit the prosecution case.
10. The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at various public places but never raised an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
The conduct of the victim shows that she was a consenting party.
11. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
12. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
13. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant-Sarfaran @ Sarfan @ Saif Ali be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

Order Date :- 18.9.2023 Vandit  Sarfaran@ Sarfan @ Saif Ali vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196932966/
